history.dynasty: Chola (8th century foundations); later renovations under Nayaks and Marathas
history.period: 8th century CE onwards; inscriptions from Chola, Nayak and Maratha periods
history.summary: One of the 108 Divya Desams, revered in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham by Tirumazhisai Alwar in two hymns. The moolavar Sundararaja Perumal reclines over Adisesha with Sridevi, Bhoodevi and Brahma in the sanctum; the festive image is worshipped as Vadivazhagiya Nambi. The temple is thronged by devotees praying for marriage. IDENTITY FLAG: the row's name 'Sri Vadivazhagiya Nambi Perumal Temple' identifies this as the Thiru Anbil Divya Desam (Sundararaja Perumal), NOT Thiruvellarai — the Thiruvellarai Divya Desam is dedicated to Pundarikakshan and is a different temple (see templenet df004 consulted for disambiguation). CSV TOWN FLAG: town corrected from Srirangam to Anbil (Lalgudi taluk, on the banks of the Kollidam, ~15-20 km east of Tiruchirappalli).

name: Sri Vadivazhagiya Nambi Perumal Temple
town_description: Anbil (Thiru Anbil) is a village in Lalgudi taluk of Tiruchirappalli district on the banks of the Kollidam river, east of Tiruchirappalli. It is known almost entirely for its ancient Divya Desam, the Sundararaja Perumal temple, reached by decent roads along the river.

travel.airport: Tiruchirappalli International Airport, about 30 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Lalgudi railway station, about 10 km away (verify).
travel.road: On the main road along the Kollidam river banks; easy to locate by road from Tiruchirappalli.

visitor_information.best_time: November to March; Vaikunta Ekadasi and Panguni Uthiram are the major festival times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 5:00 PM-8:00 PM (single traveller source - verify before visiting).
